prayerExcerpt.en-US: The thought of the world to come will always make us happy, and yet strict with ourselves in all our duties.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: O pensamento do mundo vindouro sempre nos fará felizes, e contudo rigorosos conosco mesmos em todos os nossos deveres.

meta.face: An Irishman of about seventy-five, CLEAN-SHAVEN, with a fair, fine-skinned complexion lit by a RUDDY GLOW, the front of the head shaved from EAR TO EAR in the Irish tonsure so that a smooth, bare forehead rises high, and long, fine WHITE hair falls from the back of the head to the shoulders; a BROAD, OPEN face, as WIDE at the jaw as at the cheekbones, with SMOOTH, FULL, glowing cheeks and no hollows — a straight, medium nose with a slightly UPTURNED tip, very LARGE, clear, luminous light-grey eyes set wide apart under faint, high, white brows, a WIDE, generous mouth in a joyful smile, and a firm chin with a distinct CLEFT; the gaze lifted a little, radiant ('angelic in appearance').
meta.basis: No likeness survives. Adomnán's Life (Reeves's translation, 1874) calls him 'angelic in appearance', with 'a holy joy ever beaming on his face', and tells his face suffused 'with a ruddy glow' at Mass; Reeves's introduction says his order kept the Irish tonsure 'from ear to ear' until 718. Karl Parsons's 1913 window shows him clean-shaven, tonsured, with a dove. The book tells the founder of Iona, apostle of the Picts, dying at seventy-seven in 597. The broad, open face with the cleft chin is our choice.
